five_minutes: Federal Reserve rate decision and dot plot projections this week will set the path for global yields and FII flows into emerging markets.
Escalating Middle East geopolitical tension risks pushing Brent crude toward $120, threatening India's import costs and inflation outlook.
Persistent Indian retail price inflation restricts RBI's scope to shift toward monetary easing, keeping local yields elevated.
RBI's ₹1 lakh crore OMO sales starting September 17 and ₹5 lakh crore VRRR auction reinforce systemic liquidity absorption.
The upcoming ₹22,500 crore NSE IPO will test primary market demand while pulling liquidity from secondary domestic equities.

theses.thesis: Crypto is rising because markets expect a global recession (crypto trading as the recession hedge)
US policy decisions under Trump are pushing the US economy toward decline, contrary to the stated growth narrative
theses.note: Trump's policy moves to eliminate Irish whiskey tariffs and reject AI regulatory restrictions support trade and tech investment.

theses.thesis: Gold and silver will NOT rise further even in a recession, because they are already at all-time highs
Nifty 29-Sep futures will fall below 23,000 before expiry
theses.note: Persistent Indian inflation, elevated oil supply risks, and liquidity absorption from NSE's massive IPO weigh on domestic equity market sentiment.

buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: Upcoming Fed rate decision and dot plot projections will set the path for global yields and USD strength
items.what_happened: Federal Reserve officials prepare to release updated economic projections, inflation expectations, and the interest rate dot plot at their upcoming rate decision.
items.why_it_matters: The Fed's dot plot will signal the magnitude and speed of US monetary easing. A hawkish repricing would strengthen the US dollar, widen rate differentials, and pressure FII flows out of Indian equities and debt.
items.action: Review foreign portfolio investment positioning and dollar exposure ahead of the FOMC rate release.

items.headline: US rejection of AI regulatory limits maintains momentum for global technology capital expenditure
items.what_happened: President Trump dismissed warnings over AI risks as concerns from negative forces, emphasizing technological competition against China.
items.why_it_matters: The explicit US refusal to impose federal AI development restrictions clears regulatory friction for mega-cap tech capex. This supports global technology sector earnings and hardware supply chain valuations.

items.headline: Sticky domestic retail inflation restricts RBI's flexibility to transition toward monetary policy easing
items.what_happened: Key inflation data indicates that price pressures in India remain persistent, challenging expectations of early monetary easing.
items.why_it_matters: Persistent price pressures keep real interest rates elevated and delay RBI rate cuts. This maintains high borrowing costs for domestic banks, corporate issuers, and real estate developers.

items.headline: EU's concessional duty quota for Indian vehicles opens long-term export channels for domestic auto manufacturers
items.what_happened: Under a trade agreement, the European Union will allow 2.5 lakh Indian passenger vehicles annually at a reduced 8% duty, gradually phasing to 0% over five years alongside EV quotas.
items.why_it_matters: Lowering tariffs from standard levels opens structural export opportunities for Indian auto exporters and EV component supply chains, boosting manufacturing earnings outlooks.

items.headline: RBI schedules ₹1 lakh crore OMO bond sales in three tranches from Sep 17, reinforcing long-term liquidity drain
items.what_happened: The RBI detailed its OMO sale auction schedule for ₹1,00,000 crore in three tranches (₹50,000 crore, ₹25,000 crore, and ₹25,000 crore) beginning September 17, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Continuing yesterday's liquidity management announcement, the explicit auction timeline confirms durable open market supply. The planned absorption of ₹1 lakh crore will keep medium-term G-sec yields firm and elevate corporate bond issuance spreads.

items.headline: RBI conducts ₹5 lakh crore overnight VRRR auction to absorb interbank surplus and anchor short-term rates
items.what_happened: The RBI announced a 1-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction for ₹5,00,000 crore on September 15, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Following yesterday's liquidity posture, this massive VRRR operation mops up excess overnight systemic liquidity. It keeps overnight money market rates anchored near the repo rate floor and limits short-end yield soft spots.

items.headline: NSE's ₹22,500 crore IPO launch will absorb domestic market liquidity and test secondary equity demand
items.what_happened: The National Stock Exchange announced its IPO opening on September 17 to raise an estimated ₹21,494 crore to ₹22,569 crore.
items.why_it_matters: This massive primary market issuance will absorb significant institutional and retail capital, potentially dampening secondary equity market liquidity and short-term trading volumes.
items.action: Monitor secondary market liquidity and mutual fund cash allocations during the subscription window.

items.headline: SEBI issues operational FAQ for Demat 2.0 tokenised bond pilot, clarifying digital settlement mechanics
items.what_happened: SEBI published an operational FAQ detailing the implementation of its Demat 2.0 pilot project for tokenised corporate bonds.
items.why_it_matters: Advancing yesterday's pilot launch, the guidance clarifies settlement timelines and custody structures for tokenised debt instruments, supporting secondary market transparency in corporate bonds.

items.headline: Government schedules ₹24,000 crore T-bill auction to meet short-term cash requirements
items.what_happened: The RBI announced an auction of 91-day (₹9,000 cr), 182-day (₹8,000 cr), and 364-day (₹7,000 cr) Treasury Bills totaling ₹24,000 crore on September 16, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Regular short-term debt supply establishes the short-end risk-free curve, anchoring commercial paper and bank certificate of deposit rates.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: RBI's FEMA circular rationalisation simplifies cross-border compliance for Indian corporates and authorized dealers
items.what_happened: The RBI issued a circular updating and rationalising existing regulations under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999.
items.why_it_matters: Following up on ongoing regulatory streamlining, the simplified FEMA rules reduce compliance complexity for cross-border investments, outward remittances, and foreign bank account operations.
items.action: Review cross-border remittance advisories for corporate clients against the updated FEMA circulars.

items.headline: RBI draft KYC amendment mandates standardized bank SOPs for freezing and handling money mule accounts
items.what_happened: The RBI released draft KYC amendment directions establishing a Standard Operating Procedure for action against bank accounts identified as money mules, following Supreme Court instructions.
items.why_it_matters: Continuing yesterday's proposal, the draft SOP sets legal guidelines for account freezes and operations. Banking and NBFC compliance teams must update internal audit trails and fraud detection protocols.

items.headline: RBI updates Priority Sector Lending guidelines, altering classification rules for commercial banks and SFBs
items.what_happened: The RBI released the Priority Sector Lending Third Amendment Directions 2026, revising targets and classification rules.
items.why_it_matters: Changes to PSL classification affect bank compliance mandates, credit distribution strategies, and the pricing of Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs) among commercial lenders.
items.action: Audit bank client credit portfolios against the newly revised PSL classification criteria.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: Escalating Middle East conflict threatens oil rally toward $120, expanding India's energy import burden
items.what_happened: Deepening geopolitical conflicts in the Middle East heighten supply disruption risks, raising fears of crude oil surging to $120 per barrel.
items.why_it_matters: A sustained oil price surge directly swells India's current account deficit, drives up domestic input costs, and limits the RBI's ability to lower benchmark rates. Watch Brent crude prices closely as imported inflation risks re-emerge.

items.headline: Benchmark 2033 G-sec cut-off yield firms at 6.82% amid heavy government borrowing supply
items.what_happened: The RBI completed sovereign bond auctions where the 6.57% GS 2033 paper cut off at ₹98.36, setting a yield to maturity of 6.82%.
items.why_it_matters: Building on yesterday's benchmark auction, the cut-off confirms persistent yield pressure at 6.82% for 10-year paper. High sovereign yields set a high floor for corporate debt repricing across banking and infrastructure balance sheets.
